text:
alex: Heads-up — during canary fleet run I saw a short window of stale reads after a prefix handback. Only a few requests but reproducible in run #7.

devon: Can you paste logs / repro?

alex: Minimal snippet:
```
2025-02-14T11:12:05Z INFO prefix-handoff tenant=acme prefix=org:123 handback_epoch=42 observed_epoch=40 read_latency_ms=12
2025-02-14T11:12:05Z WARN kv-read tenant=acme prefix=org:123 key=k1 value_stale=true source=local_cache
```

maria: Two quick guesses: (A) the handback didn't surface the new visibility epoch to readers, (B) some read-path cached an old generation token and never revalidated.

sam: Is there currently an explicit persisted "visible_epoch" or is visibility implicit in the lease token?

alex: It's implicit. We embed epoch in lease tokens and rely on best-effort distribution. That design allows a tiny divergence window when tokens move.

jing: Alternatives we discussed in the RFC followup: 1) make visible_epoch explicit + durable (CAS on ownership store), 2) keep tokens but add monotonic generation id and cheap revalidate RPC for mismatches, 3) accept short divergence and run background repair / read-repair.

devon: Durable CAS is easiest conceptually but adds a write on handback. How frequent are these transfers in rebalance?

alex: Under steady state very rare; during rebalances spikes of O(10/s) per cluster are plausible. CAS-per-transfer could be fine if we batch or rate-limit, but need to benchmark.

maria: What about hybrid policy: require CAS only when the transfer crosses nodes (i.e., changes topology). Intra-node handbacks can bump an in-memory epoch and broadcast a visibility update. Readers do local-check-first and RPC only on mismatch.

sam: That seems sensible. Also we must make epochs strictly monotonic and include a node id tie-breaker so out-of-order broadcasts don't regress visibility.

jing: Implementation sketch:
```
// on handback
if (cross_node_transfer) {
  ownership_store.CAS(prefix, old_epoch, new_epoch)
} else {
  local_epoch = new_epoch
  broadcast(visibility_update(prefix, new_epoch, origin_node_id))
}

// on read
if (local_epoch_hint < canonical_epoch_hint) {
  async revalidate(prefix) // cheap RPC to owner or ring state
}
```

devon: For broadcasting we need ordering guarantees; include epoch+node-id and accept only updates with newer epoch||(same_epoch and higher node id). Also add a short TTL on tokens so stale clients eventually expire rather than relying on revalidation forever.

alex: Agreed. TTL on tokens helps long-lived cursors. We'll also require cursors to refresh token after TTL.

maria: Ops constraints: keep the fast-path zero-RPC. Local-check-first, RPC on mismatch. Also add sampled revalidations to measure correctness.

sam: Telemetry proposal: emit prefix_visibility_lag_ms histogram, node_observed_epoch gauge, and sampled_revalidate counter. Alert if >0.5% reads need revalidate or if p99 lag > 200ms.

jing: Migration plan: telemetry-only first (shadow CAS + logs), canary the broadcast approach, then opt-in CAS for cross-node transfers, finally flip enforcement. Have rollback plan: if CAS contention spikes, fallback to background repair + exponential backoff.

alex: Perf action: devon to bench CAS write latency and throughput under synthetic rebalance (10-50 handbacks/s). If write QPS looks fine we can proceed.

devon: I'll run microbench Wednesday against staging ownership store and report tail latencies.

maria: Action items:
- alex: open canary PR with added handback traces and broadcast pilot
- devon: CAS prototype + perf job
- jing: telemetry proto + dashboards
- sam: ops runbook + alert thresholds

sre-bot: Created alert ENG-RUNTIME-PFX-VIS-LAG threshold=200ms p99 scope=production

alex: Edge case: long-lived cursors that never refresh. We'll add token_ttl and emit cursor_refresh_required metric so apps can be signalled.

maria: Documentation: append a short section to the design doc summarizing why implicit tokens were insufficient and how the hybrid CAS/broadcast approach fixes it. Keep the fast path unchanged for latency.

sam: I'll add these tasks to the prefix/evict epic and mark staging perf as blocker for full rollout.

jing: Drafting rollback text in the PR in case CAS causes repeated contention — fallback to broadcast+repair and pause enforcement rollouts.

alex: Sounds good. I'll ping the canary when PR is ready.

maria: Acknowledged — I'll prepare dashboard panels and runbook snippet.

devon: Bench start Wed.

alex: Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
